events.explanation: The DataFrame.append() method was removed in pandas 3.1.0. The notebook already uses pd.concat() in cells 7-15 for the same operation. Cell 16 tries to use the deprecated df1.append(df2) syntax which no longer exists. The fix replaces it with the equivalent pd.concat([df1, df2]) call.

sources.title: What’s new in 3.1.0 (Month XX, 2026) — pandas 3.2.0.dev0 documentation
sources.content:
Deprecated the `dropna` keyword in `DataFrame.to_hdf()`, `HDFStore.put()`, `HDFStore.append()`, and `HDFStore.append_to_multiple()`, and the `io.hdf.dropna_table` option. Use `DataFrame.dropna()` before writing instead (GH 32038)
 Deprecated the `float_precision` argument in `read_csv()`, `read_table()`, and `read_fwf()`. All float precision modes now use the same converter (GH 64395) [...] `HDFStore.append()` now raises `TypeError` when the appended data is timezone-aware and the stored column is timezone-naive, or vice versa; such an append was previously accepted and the rows already on disk were read back as different timestamps (GH 68583) [...] `HDFStore.append()` now raises `TypeError` when the appended index and the stored one disagree about being a `PeriodIndex`, or are both `PeriodIndex` with a different `freq`; such an append was previously accepted and the rows already on disk were read back as the wrong values (GH 68523)

sources.content:
•2y ago

I believe it's been replaced by pandas.concat - concatenate 2 DF's together.

you will have to change the code , and the syntax is a little different (in that you concatenate both DF's using the function, rather than appending one to the other.

eg:

df1=pd.concat([df1, df2])

 Reply  Share 

Image 9: u/Waterbottles_solve avatar

Waterbottles_solve

•2y ago

Yes.

Are the parameters drop-in too?

 Reply  Share [...] There's no way to append a row to a dataframe because the omniscients at Pandas said "there's no use case for it". [...] Reply  Share 


df is the first dataframe, and temp_df is appended to the end of the df in this example. Axis is how the data is appended. axis=0 is vertical append (end of df), and 1 is appending horizontally (to the right side of rows) if memory serves. You'll need to update everywhere .append() is used, unfortunately. Hope this helps.

sources.title: Pandas’ 2.0 Release Deprecated Your Favorite Method. What Now?
sources.content: One of my favorite functions in Pandas (and yeah, I realize how nerdy it is to have a favorite function), is the .append() method. For someone in my role who spends most days interacting with APIs returning data in different forms, .append() is a quickly implemented catch-all solution when it comes to creating a data frame from a list of dicts within a JSON payload, which is common in API-based data sources.
